plain: From the late 1940s, bright green fireballs were seen streaking over New Mexico, and an official investigation called Project Twinkle was set up to study them. A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb describes it on the show as an investigation run by the 'Z division' of Sandia, a government laboratory in New Mexico, and points to the project's own records. Michels tells it himself on two other episodes. He calls it 'an Air Force investigation' and says it was headed by Lincoln LaPaz, a meteor expert at the University of New Mexico, who began tracking the fireballs. In one telling Michels says the fireballs were 'showing up across American nuclear sites', naming Los Alamos and Holloman Air Force Base. In another he cites FBI documents on the fireballs. So the tellers differ on whose project it was, Sandia's or the Air Force's, but they agree on LaPaz and the green lights. They tell it because, if true, something unexplained kept turning up over the country's most sensitive nuclear sites.
